During the **Parade of Nations** portion of the 2004 Summer Olympics opening ceremony, athletes from each country participating in the Olympics paraded in the arena, preceded by their flag. The flag was borne by a sportsperson from that country chosen either by the [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") or by the athletes themselves to represent their country.

## Parade order

The national team of Greece, as the host nation, entered the stadium last, breaking the tradition that the Greece national team enter first in every Olympic opening ceremony as a tribute for being the original host of both the Ancient and the Modern Olympic Games. However, in a nod to tradition, the Greek flag and flag bearer [Pyrros Dimas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrros_Dimas "Pyrros Dimas") entered at the beginning of the parade ahead of [Saint Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia "Saint Lucia"), to avoid breaking the tradition entirely. Dimas also led the Greece national team when they entered last. Following tradition, other countries entered the stadium in name order in the language of the host country (Greece), which in this case is [Modern Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Greek "Modern Greek").

[Kiribati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiribati "Kiribati") and [Timor-Leste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timor-Leste "Timor-Leste") competed for the first time at these Olympic Games, whereas [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan") returned from its eight-year absence after the national Olympic committee had been suspended under the [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban") regime since 1999.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_national_flag_bearers?printable=yes#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_national_flag_bearers?printable=yes#cite_note-2) The parade of nations also featured a unified entrance by the athletes of the North and South Korea, holding a specially designed [unification flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_flag "Unification flag") bearing the name "Korea" (Κορέα): a white background flag with a blue map of the Korean peninsula; however, the two teams competed separately.

Announcers in the stadium read off the names of the marching nations in [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"), French, and English (the official languages of the host country and of the Olympics, respectively) with the music, performed and played by Dutch musician [Tiësto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%C3%ABsto "Tiësto"), accompanying the athletes as they marched into the stadium.

Whilst most countries entered under their [short names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states "List of sovereign states"), a few entered under more formal or alternative names, mostly due to political and naming disputes. The [Republic of Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Macedonia "Republic of Macedonia") entered as the "**F**ormer Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'" ("**Π**ρώην Γιουγκοσλαβική Δημοκρατία της Μακεδονίας") under Π because of the [naming dispute with Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macedonia_naming_dispute "Macedonia naming dispute"). The [Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China "Republic of China") (commonly known as Taiwan) entered with the compromised [name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Taipei "Chinese Taipei") and [flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Taipei_Olympic_flag "Chinese Taipei Olympic flag") of "Chinese **T**aipei" ("Κινεζικη **Τ**αϊπεϊ") under Τ so that they did not enter together with [conflicting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_Chinas "Two Chinas")[People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") (commonly known as China), which entered as the "People's Republic of **C**hina" ("Λαϊκή Δημοκρατία της **Κ**ίνας") under Κ. The [Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Congo "Republic of the Congo") entered as just "**C**ongo" (**Κ**ονγκό), while the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo") entered with its full name, "Λαϊκή **Δ**ημοκρατία του Κονγκό" under Δ. The [**B**ritish Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Virgin_Islands "British Virgin Islands") ("**Β**ρετανικές Παρθένοι Νήσοι") entered under Β while the [United States Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands") entered as simply the "**V**irgin Islands" ("**Π**αρθένοι Νήσοι"), under Π. Additionally, [Ivory Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory_Coast "Ivory Coast"), the United States, [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), [Laos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laos "Laos"), [Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya "Libya"), Russia, [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") and Hong Kong all entered under their formal names, respectively "**C**ôte d'Ivoire", the "**U**nited States of America", "Islamic Republic of **I**ran", "**L**ao People's Democratic Republic", "**L**ibyan Arab Jamahiriya", "**R**ussian Federation", "**S**yrian Arab Republic" and "**H**ong Kong, China".

Notable flag bearers in the opening ceremony featured the following athletes: triple Grand Slam champion and tennis player [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer") (Switzerland), NBA basketball player [Yao Ming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yao_Ming "Yao Ming") (People's Republic of China), six-time Olympians and Star sailors [Colin Beashel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Beashel "Colin Beashel") (Australia) and [Torben Grael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torben_Grael "Torben Grael") (Brazil), triple Olympic weightlifting champion [Pyrros Dimas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrros_Dimas "Pyrros Dimas") (Greece), show jumper [Ludger Beerbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludger_Beerbaum "Ludger Beerbaum") (Germany), two-time Olympic sprint freestyle champion [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)") (Russia), four-time rowing champion [Elisabeta Lipă](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisabeta_Lip%C4%83 "Elisabeta Lipă") (Romania), decathlon champion [Erki Nool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erki_Nool "Erki Nool") (Estonia), and rings gymnast [Jury Chechi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jury_Chechi "Jury Chechi") (Italy).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_national_flag_bearers?printable=yes#cite_note-olympic-flag-bearers-3)

During the **Parade of Nations** portion of the 2004 Summer Olympics opening ceremony, athletes from each country participating in the Olympics paraded in the arena, preceded by their flag. The flag was borne by a sportsperson from that country chosen either by the [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") or by the athletes themselves to represent their country.

## Parade order

The national team of Greece, as the host nation, entered the stadium last, breaking the tradition that the Greece national team enter first in every Olympic opening ceremony as a tribute for being the original host of both the Ancient and the Modern Olympic Games. However, in a nod to tradition, the Greek flag and flag bearer [Pyrros Dimas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrros_Dimas "Pyrros Dimas") entered at the beginning of the parade ahead of [Saint Lucia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Lucia "Saint Lucia"), to avoid breaking the tradition entirely. Dimas also led the Greece national team when they entered last. Following tradition, other countries entered the stadium in name order in the language of the host country (Greece), which in this case is [Modern Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Greek "Modern Greek").

[Kiribati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiribati "Kiribati") and [Timor-Leste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timor-Leste "Timor-Leste") competed for the first time at these Olympic Games, whereas [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afghanistan "Afghanistan") returned from its eight-year absence after the national Olympic committee had been suspended under the [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban") regime since 1999.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_national_flag_bearers?printable=yes#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_national_flag_bearers?printable=yes#cite_note-2) The parade of nations also featured a unified entrance by the athletes of the North and South Korea, holding a specially designed [unification flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_flag "Unification flag") bearing the name "Korea" (Κορέα): a white background flag with a blue map of the Korean peninsula; however, the two teams competed separately.

Announcers in the stadium read off the names of the marching nations in [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"), French, and English (the official languages of the host country and of the Olympics, respectively) with the music, performed and played by Dutch musician [Tiësto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti%C3%ABsto "Tiësto"), accompanying the athletes as they marched into the stadium.

Whilst most countries entered under their [short names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states "List of sovereign states"), a few entered under more formal or alternative names, mostly due to political and naming disputes. The [Republic of Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Macedonia "Republic of Macedonia") entered as the "**F**ormer Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'" ("**Π**ρώην Γιουγκοσλαβική Δημοκρατία της Μακεδονίας") under Π because of the [naming dispute with Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macedonia_naming_dispute "Macedonia naming dispute"). The [Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China "Republic of China") (commonly known as Taiwan) entered with the compromised [name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Taipei "Chinese Taipei") and [flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Taipei_Olympic_flag "Chinese Taipei Olympic flag") of "Chinese **T**aipei" ("Κινεζικη **Τ**αϊπεϊ") under Τ so that they did not enter together with [conflicting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_Chinas "Two Chinas")[People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") (commonly known as China), which entered as the "People's Republic of **C**hina" ("Λαϊκή Δημοκρατία της **Κ**ίνας") under Κ. The [Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Congo "Republic of the Congo") entered as just "**C**ongo" (**Κ**ονγκό), while the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_the_Congo "Democratic Republic of the Congo") entered with its full name, "Λαϊκή **Δ**ημοκρατία του Κονγκό" under Δ. The [**B**ritish Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Virgin_Islands "British Virgin Islands") ("**Β**ρετανικές Παρθένοι Νήσοι") entered under Β while the [United States Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands") entered as simply the "**V**irgin Islands" ("**Π**αρθένοι Νήσοι"), under Π. Additionally, [Ivory Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivory_Coast "Ivory Coast"), the United States, [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), [Laos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laos "Laos"), [Libya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya "Libya"), Russia, [Syria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria "Syria") and Hong Kong all entered under their formal names, respectively "**C**ôte d'Ivoire", the "**U**nited States of America", "Islamic Republic of **I**ran", "**L**ao People's Democratic Republic", "**L**ibyan Arab Jamahiriya", "**R**ussian Federation", "**S**yrian Arab Republic" and "**H**ong Kong, China".

Notable flag bearers in the opening ceremony featured the following athletes: triple Grand Slam champion and tennis player [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer") (Switzerland), NBA basketball player [Yao Ming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yao_Ming "Yao Ming") (People's Republic of China), six-time Olympians and Star sailors [Colin Beashel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Beashel "Colin Beashel") (Australia) and [Torben Grael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torben_Grael "Torben Grael") (Brazil), triple Olympic weightlifting champion [Pyrros Dimas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyrros_Dimas "Pyrros Dimas") (Greece), show jumper [Ludger Beerbaum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludger_Beerbaum "Ludger Beerbaum") (Germany), two-time Olympic sprint freestyle champion [Alexander Popov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Popov_(swimmer) "Alexander Popov (swimmer)") (Russia), four-time rowing champion [Elisabeta Lipă](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elisabeta_Lip%C4%83 "Elisabeta Lipă") (Romania), decathlon champion [Erki Nool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erki_Nool "Erki Nool") (Estonia), and rings gymnast [Jury Chechi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jury_Chechi "Jury Chechi") (Italy).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_national_flag_bearers?printable=yes#cite_note-olympic-flag-bearers-3)

**Violet Awindi Barasa** (Born June 21, 1975, [Sikhendu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhendu?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sikhendu (page does not exist)") village, [Webuye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webuye "Webuye"), [Bungoma District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungoma_District "Bungoma District"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") , ) was a [volleyball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball "Volleyball") player from [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Her surname is sometimes spelled as **Baraza**.

She was a long-time captain for the [Kenyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") women's national volleyball team. Baraza represented Kenya in the [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Volleyball at the 2000 Summer Olympics") and [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Volleyball at the 2000 Summer Olympics") Olympic Games, three times in the [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIVB_Volleyball_Women's_World_Championship "FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship") and in numerous continental events.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-1)

## Life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life")]

Barasa was born in 1975 and she attended Lugulu High School which is known for its support for volleyball. She began by playing volleyball for the [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank "Kenya Commercial Bank") and from there she was included in [Kenya women's national volleyball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_women's_national_volleyball_team "Kenya women's national volleyball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-vibiog-2)

She was one of the few Kenyan players to play professional volleyball abroad, for [Al Ahly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ahly_(volleyball) "Al Ahly (volleyball)") in [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), Vileo and Unic-Romania in [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania"), Panellinios in [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") and Dicle University in [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-3)

As national team captain she led the national team to its appearances at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") and the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-vibiog-2)

She died in February 2007 at the Webuye District Hospital of undisclosed causes. At the time of her death, she was still an active player with the [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank_S.C. "Kenya Commercial Bank S.C.") volleyball club, although she had been dropped from the national team. After her death volleyball matches were postponed in Kenya until after her funeral as a mark of respect.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-vibiog-2)

**Violet Awindi Barasa** (Born June 21, 1975, [Sikhendu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhendu?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sikhendu (page does not exist)") village, [Webuye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webuye "Webuye"), [Bungoma District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungoma_District "Bungoma District"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") , ) was a [volleyball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball "Volleyball") player from [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Her surname is sometimes spelled as **Baraza**.

She was a long-time captain for the [Kenyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") women's national volleyball team. Baraza represented Kenya in the [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Volleyball at the 2000 Summer Olympics") and [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Volleyball at the 2000 Summer Olympics") Olympic Games, three times in the [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIVB_Volleyball_Women's_World_Championship "FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship") and in numerous continental events.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-1)

## Life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life")]

Barasa was born in 1975 and she attended Lugulu High School which is known for its support for volleyball. She began by playing volleyball for the [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank "Kenya Commercial Bank") and from there she was included in [Kenya women's national volleyball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_women's_national_volleyball_team "Kenya women's national volleyball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-vibiog-2)

She was one of the few Kenyan players to play professional volleyball abroad, for [Al Ahly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ahly_(volleyball) "Al Ahly (volleyball)") in [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), Vileo and Unic-Romania in [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania"), Panellinios in [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") and Dicle University in [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-3)

As national team captain she led the national team to its appearances at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") and the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-vibiog-2)

She died in February 2007 at the Webuye District Hospital of undisclosed causes. At the time of her death, she was still an active player with the [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank_S.C. "Kenya Commercial Bank S.C.") volleyball club, although she had been dropped from the national team. After her death volleyball matches were postponed in Kenya until after her funeral as a mark of respect.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Violet_Barasa#cite_note-vibiog-2)

**Davis Mwale** (born May 8, 1972) is a [boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing") from [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia "Zambia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Mwale#cite_note-1)

He participated in the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the 2004 Summer Olympics") for his native [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") country. There he was stopped in the second round of the [Light welterweight (64 kg) division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Light_welterweight "Boxing at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Light welterweight") by [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba")'s eventual runner-up [Yudel Johnson Cedeno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yudel_Johnson_Cedeno "Yudel Johnson Cedeno").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Mwale won the bronze medal in the same division one year earlier, at the [All-Africa Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2003_All-Africa_Games "Boxing at the 2003 All-Africa Games") in [Abuja, Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abuja,_Nigeria "Abuja, Nigeria").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

**Davis Mwale** (born May 8, 1972) is a [boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing") from [Zambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zambia "Zambia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Mwale#cite_note-1)

He participated in the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the 2004 Summer Olympics") for his native [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa") country. There he was stopped in the second round of the [Light welterweight (64 kg) division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Light_welterweight "Boxing at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Light welterweight") by [Cuba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba "Cuba")'s eventual runner-up [Yudel Johnson Cedeno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yudel_Johnson_Cedeno "Yudel Johnson Cedeno").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Mwale won the bronze medal in the same division one year earlier, at the [All-Africa Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_at_the_2003_All-Africa_Games "Boxing at the 2003 All-Africa Games") in [Abuja, Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abuja,_Nigeria "Abuja, Nigeria").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

**Kennedy Ochieng** (born 31 December 1971) is a retired Kenyan sprinter who specialised in the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/400_metres "400 metres") and competed at the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") and [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kennedy_Ochieng&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Ochieng won the British [AAA Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAA_Championships "AAA Championships") title in the 400 metres event at the [1993 AAA Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_AAA_Championships "1993 AAA Championships").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-3)

He was the flagbearer for [Kenya at the 2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Kenya at the 2000 Summer Olympics") in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-oly-4)

**Kennedy Ochieng** (born 31 December 1971) is a retired Kenyan sprinter who specialised in the [400 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/400_metres "400 metres") and competed at the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") and [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-1)

## Biography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kennedy_Ochieng&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Biography")]

Ochieng won the British [AAA Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAA_Championships "AAA Championships") title in the 400 metres event at the [1993 AAA Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_AAA_Championships "1993 AAA Championships").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-3)

He was the flagbearer for [Kenya at the 2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Kenya at the 2000 Summer Olympics") in [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Ochieng#cite_note-oly-4)

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

Tanzania was represented at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), Greece by the [Tanzania Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_Olympic_Committee "Tanzania Olympic Committee").

In total, eight athletes including six men and two women represented Tanzania in one sport: athletics.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Tanganyika was represented at the [1964 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan by what would become the [Tanzania Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_Olympic_Committee "Tanzania Olympic Committee"). After the unification of Tanganyika and Zanzibar to form the United Republic of Tanzania, the country made its debut at the [1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics "1968 Summer Olympics") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"), Mexico. They have appeared at every games since except the [1976 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics "1976 Summer Olympics") in [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal "Montreal"), [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec"), Canada after they took part in the [African boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1976 Summer Olympics boycott"). The [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), Greece marked Tanzania's ninth appearance at the Summer Olympics. Prior to 2004, they had only won two medals – both silver – at the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), [Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic"), Soviet Union.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-2)

## Athletics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Athletics")]

Main article: [Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics")

In total, eight Tanzanian athletes participated in the athletics events – [Samwel Mwera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samwel_Mwera "Samwel Mwera") in the [800 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_800_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 800 metres") and the [1,500 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_1500_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 1500 metres"), [Fabiano Joseph Naasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabiano_Joseph_Naasi "Fabiano Joseph Naasi") in the [men's 5,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 5000 metres") and the [men's 10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres"), [Restituta Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restituta_Joseph "Restituta Joseph") in the [women's 5,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres"), [John Yuda Msuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Yuda_Msuri "John Yuda Msuri") in the men's 10,000 m, [Zebedayo Bayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zebedayo_Bayo "Zebedayo Bayo"), [Samson Ramadhani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samson_Ramadhani "Samson Ramadhani") and [John Nada Saya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Nada_Saya "John Nada Saya") in the [men's marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [Banuelia Mrashani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banuelia_Mrashani "Banuelia Mrashani") in the [women's marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_marathon "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's marathon").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-tanzania-3)

Most of the athletics events took place at the [Athens Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Athens) "Olympic Stadium (Athens)") in [Marousi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marousi "Marousi"), Athens from 18 to 29 August 2004.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-4) The men's and women's marathons took place at the [Panathenaic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathenaic_Stadium "Panathenaic Stadium") in [Pangrati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangrati "Pangrati"), Athens.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-5)

Tanzania was represented at the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), Greece by the [Tanzania Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_Olympic_Committee "Tanzania Olympic Committee").

In total, eight athletes including six men and two women represented Tanzania in one sport: athletics.

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Tanganyika was represented at the [1964 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics") in [Tokyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo "Tokyo"), Japan by what would become the [Tanzania Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_Olympic_Committee "Tanzania Olympic Committee"). After the unification of Tanganyika and Zanzibar to form the United Republic of Tanzania, the country made its debut at the [1968 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics "1968 Summer Olympics") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City"), Mexico. They have appeared at every games since except the [1976 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics "1976 Summer Olympics") in [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal "Montreal"), [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec"), Canada after they took part in the [African boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics_boycott "1976 Summer Olympics boycott"). The [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens"), Greece marked Tanzania's ninth appearance at the Summer Olympics. Prior to 2004, they had only won two medals – both silver – at the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics") in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), [Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic"), Soviet Union.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-2)

## Athletics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Athletics")]

Main article: [Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics")

In total, eight Tanzanian athletes participated in the athletics events – [Samwel Mwera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samwel_Mwera "Samwel Mwera") in the [800 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_800_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 800 metres") and the [1,500 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_1500_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 1500 metres"), [Fabiano Joseph Naasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fabiano_Joseph_Naasi "Fabiano Joseph Naasi") in the [men's 5,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 5000 metres") and the [men's 10,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_10,000_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's 10,000 metres"), [Restituta Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Restituta_Joseph "Restituta Joseph") in the [women's 5,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_5000_metres "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's 5000 metres"), [John Yuda Msuri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Yuda_Msuri "John Yuda Msuri") in the men's 10,000 m, [Zebedayo Bayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zebedayo_Bayo "Zebedayo Bayo"), [Samson Ramadhani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samson_Ramadhani "Samson Ramadhani") and [John Nada Saya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Nada_Saya "John Nada Saya") in the [men's marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Men's_marathon "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's marathon") and [Banuelia Mrashani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banuelia_Mrashani "Banuelia Mrashani") in the [women's marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_marathon "Athletics at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Women's marathon").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-tanzania-3)

Most of the athletics events took place at the [Athens Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Athens) "Olympic Stadium (Athens)") in [Marousi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marousi "Marousi"), Athens from 18 to 29 August 2004.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-4) The men's and women's marathons took place at the [Panathenaic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathenaic_Stadium "Panathenaic Stadium") in [Pangrati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pangrati "Pangrati"), Athens.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics#cite_note-5)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice [carried the flag for Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_Tanzania_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for Tanzania at the Olympics") at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice [carried the flag for Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_Tanzania_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for Tanzania at the Olympics") at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

**Violet Awindi Barasa** (Born June 21, 1975, [Sikhendu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhendu?action=edit&redlink=1 "Sikhendu (page does not exist)") village, [Webuye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webuye "Webuye"), [Bungoma District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungoma_District "Bungoma District"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") , ) was a [volleyball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball "Volleyball") player from [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Her surname is sometimes spelled as **Baraza**.

She was a long-time captain for the [Kenyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") women's national volleyball team. Baraza represented Kenya in the [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Volleyball at the 2000 Summer Olympics") and [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volleyball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Volleyball at the 2000 Summer Olympics") Olympic Games, three times in the [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIVB_Volleyball_Women's_World_Championship "FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship") and in numerous continental events.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&printable=yes#cite_note-1)

## Life

Barasa was born in 1975 and she attended Lugulu High School which is known for its support for volleyball. She began by playing volleyball for the [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank "Kenya Commercial Bank") and from there she was included in [Kenya women's national volleyball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_women's_national_volleyball_team "Kenya women's national volleyball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&printable=yes#cite_note-vibiog-2)

She was one of the few Kenyan players to play professional volleyball abroad, for [Al Ahly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ahly_(volleyball) "Al Ahly (volleyball)") in [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), Vileo and Unic-Romania in [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania "Romania"), Panellinios in [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") and Dicle University in [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&printable=yes#cite_note-3)

As national team captain she led the national team to its appearances at the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") and the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&printable=yes#cite_note-vibiog-2)

She died in February 2007 at the Webuye District Hospital of undisclosed causes. At the time of her death, she was still an active player with the [Kenya Commercial Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Commercial_Bank_S.C. "Kenya Commercial Bank S.C.") volleyball club, although she had been dropped from the national team. After her death volleyball matches were postponed in Kenya until after her funeral as a mark of respect.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Violet_Barasa&printable=yes#cite_note-vibiog-2)

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice carried the flag for Tanzania at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice carried the flag for Tanzania at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

**Ângelo Monteiro dos Santos Victoriano** (8 February 1968 – 13 April 2024) was an Angolan [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He was listed at 6 ft 6 in (1.98 m) and 247 lbs. (112 kg). Victoriano was inducted to the [FIBA Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "FIBA Basketball Hall of Fame") in 2023 as the second Angolan player in history.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-1) Victoriano holds the record for most [FIBA AfroBasket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_AfroBasket "FIBA AfroBasket") titles in history with eight titles, and in his club career in Angola he won eleven national championships and ten national cups.

Victoriano appeared on four Angolan [Olympic basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the Summer Olympics") teams (in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 1992 Summer Olympics"), [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_1996_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 1996 Summer Olympics"), [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics"), and [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics")), serving as captain in his final appearance.

## Playing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%C3%82ngelo_Victoriano&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Playing career")]

Born in the Maçal neighbourhood of [Luanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luanda "Luanda"), Victoriano began playing with [Petro de Luanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petro_de_Luanda_(basketball) "Petro de Luanda (basketball)") in the top division at age 14.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-:0-2) At the club level, he won a total of 11 national championship titles, one with [ASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Sport_Avia%C3%A7%C3%A3o "Atlético Sport Aviação"), four with [Petro de Luanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Petr%C3%B3leos_Luanda "Atlético Petróleos Luanda") and six with [Primeiro de Agosto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeiro_de_Agosto_Basketball "Primeiro de Agosto Basketball"). He won ten Angolan Cups, eight Super Cups and two Africa Club Championships with [Primeiro de Agosto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeiro_de_Agosto_Basketball "Primeiro de Agosto Basketball").

Victoriano was the only African player to have won eight FIBA Africa championships, ahead of [Jean-Jacques Conceição](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Jacques_Concei%C3%A7%C3%A3o "Jean-Jacques Conceição"), and [Carlos Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Almeida_(basketball) "Carlos Almeida (basketball)"), both with seven.

## Coaching career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%C3%82ngelo_Victoriano&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Coaching career")]

From 2007 to 2009, Victoriano was an assistant coach under [Luís Magalhães](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Magalh%C3%A3es "Luís Magalhães") for [Primeiro de Agosto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Primeiro_de_Agosto_(men's_basketball) "C.D. Primeiro de Agosto (men's basketball)") and won the 2009 [Unitel Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitel_Basket "Unitel Basket") title with them.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-:0-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-3)

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%C3%82ngelo_Victoriano&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal")]

Victoriano died on 13 April 2024, aged 56, in Luanda following a long illness caused by [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-:0-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-4)

His brothers, [Edmar Victoriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmar_Victoriano "Edmar Victoriano") and [Puna Victoriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justino_Victoriano "Justino Victoriano"), also played for the [Angola national basketball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angola_men's_national_basketball_team "Angola men's national basketball team").

**Ângelo Monteiro dos Santos Victoriano** (8 February 1968 – 13 April 2024) was an Angolan [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He was listed at 6 ft 6 in (1.98 m) and 247 lbs. (112 kg). Victoriano was inducted to the [FIBA Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "FIBA Basketball Hall of Fame") in 2023 as the second Angolan player in history.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-1) Victoriano holds the record for most [FIBA AfroBasket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_AfroBasket "FIBA AfroBasket") titles in history with eight titles, and in his club career in Angola he won eleven national championships and ten national cups.

Victoriano appeared on four Angolan [Olympic basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the Summer Olympics") teams (in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 1992 Summer Olympics"), [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_1996_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 1996 Summer Olympics"), [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 2000 Summer Olympics"), and [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball_at_the_2004_Summer_Olympics "Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics")), serving as captain in his final appearance.

## Playing career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%C3%82ngelo_Victoriano&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Playing career")]

Born in the Maçal neighbourhood of [Luanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luanda "Luanda"), Victoriano began playing with [Petro de Luanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petro_de_Luanda_(basketball) "Petro de Luanda (basketball)") in the top division at age 14.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-:0-2) At the club level, he won a total of 11 national championship titles, one with [ASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Sport_Avia%C3%A7%C3%A3o "Atlético Sport Aviação"), four with [Petro de Luanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Petr%C3%B3leos_Luanda "Atlético Petróleos Luanda") and six with [Primeiro de Agosto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeiro_de_Agosto_Basketball "Primeiro de Agosto Basketball"). He won ten Angolan Cups, eight Super Cups and two Africa Club Championships with [Primeiro de Agosto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primeiro_de_Agosto_Basketball "Primeiro de Agosto Basketball").

Victoriano was the only African player to have won eight FIBA Africa championships, ahead of [Jean-Jacques Conceição](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Jacques_Concei%C3%A7%C3%A3o "Jean-Jacques Conceição"), and [Carlos Almeida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Almeida_(basketball) "Carlos Almeida (basketball)"), both with seven.

## Coaching career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%C3%82ngelo_Victoriano&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Coaching career")]

From 2007 to 2009, Victoriano was an assistant coach under [Luís Magalhães](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Magalh%C3%A3es "Luís Magalhães") for [Primeiro de Agosto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Primeiro_de_Agosto_(men's_basketball) "C.D. Primeiro de Agosto (men's basketball)") and won the 2009 [Unitel Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitel_Basket "Unitel Basket") title with them.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-:0-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-3)

## Personal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=%C3%82ngelo_Victoriano&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal")]

Victoriano died on 13 April 2024, aged 56, in Luanda following a long illness caused by [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes "Diabetes").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-:0-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Victoriano#cite_note-4)

His brothers, [Edmar Victoriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmar_Victoriano "Edmar Victoriano") and [Puna Victoriano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justino_Victoriano "Justino Victoriano"), also played for the [Angola national basketball team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angola_men's_national_basketball_team "Angola men's national basketball team").

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice carried the flag for Tanzania at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice carried the flag for Tanzania at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice [carried the flag for Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_Tanzania_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for Tanzania at the Olympics") at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice [carried the flag for Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_flag_bearers_for_Tanzania_at_the_Olympics "List of flag bearers for Tanzania at the Olympics") at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice carried the flag for Tanzania at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.

Tanzanian long-distance runner

**Restituta Joseph Kemi** (born 30 July 1971 in [Singida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singida_Region "Singida Region")) is a Tanzanian [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner "Long-distance runner"). She twice carried the flag for Tanzania at the opening ceremony of the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympics "Summer Olympics"): in 2000 and 2004.

She was the 1997 and 1999 winner of the [Corrida de Langueux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrida_de_Langueux "Corrida de Langueux") race.
